questions.knowledge_point: Determining the Period of a Transformed Tangent or Cotangent Function
questions.problem: Calculate the period of the function $f(x)=-3\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{8x-\pi }{4}).$
questions.worked_solution:
Given a function of the form $y=A\operatorname{tan}⁡(Bx+C)+D,$ the period is $\frac{\pi }{B}.$

In our case, we have that

$$
f(x)=-3\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{8x-\pi }{4})=-3\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x-\frac{\pi }{4}).
$$

Therefore, $B=2,$ and so the period is $\frac{\pi }{2}.$

questions.problem: Which of the following expressions gives all of the zeros of the function $f(x)=2\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x-\frac{\pi }{6})?$ Assume that $n$ is an integer.
questions.worked_solution:
The zeros of $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡x$ are given by

$$
x=n\pi ,
$$

where $n$ is an integer.

To find the zeros of $f(x)=2\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x-\frac{\pi }{6}),$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $(2x-\frac{\pi }{6}).$ This gives

$$
2x-\frac{\pi }{6}=n\pi .
$$

Solving for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-\frac{\pi }{6} & =n\pi  \\ 2x & =n\pi +\frac{\pi }{6} \\ x & =\frac{\pi }{12}+\frac{n\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the zeros are $x=\frac{\pi }{12}+\frac{n\pi }{2},$ where $n$ is an integer.

questions.problem: Which of the following expressions gives all of the zeros of the function $f(x)=4\operatorname{cot}⁡(3x+\pi )?$ Assume that $n$ is an integer.
questions.worked_solution:
The zeros of $y=\operatorname{cot}⁡x$ are given by 

$$
x=\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi ,
$$

where $n$ is an integer.

To find the zeros of $f(x)=4\operatorname{cot}⁡(3x+\pi ),$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $(3x+\pi ).$ This gives

$$
3x+\pi =\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi .
$$

Solving for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3x+\pi  & =\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi  \\ 3x & =\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi -\pi  \\ 3x & =-\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi  \\ x & =-\frac{\pi }{6}+\frac{n\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the zeros are $x=-\frac{\pi }{6}+\frac{n\pi }{3},$ where $n$ is an integer.

questions.problem: Which of the following expressions gives all of the vertical asymptotes of the function  $f(x)=\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{\pi x}{3}+\frac{\pi }{6})?$ Assume that $n$ is an integer.
questions.worked_solution:
The asymptotes of $y=\operatorname{cot}⁡x$ are given by the expression

$$
x=n\pi ,
$$

where $n$ is an integer.

To find the asymptotes of $\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{\pi x}{3}+\frac{\pi }{6}),$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $(\frac{\pi x}{3}+\frac{\pi }{6}).$ This gives

$$
\frac{\pi x}{3}+\frac{\pi }{6}=n\pi .
$$

Solving for $x,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\pi x}{3}+\frac{\pi }{6} & =n\pi  \\ \frac{\pi x}{3} & =-\frac{\pi }{6}+n\pi  \\ \pi x & =-\frac{\pi }{2}+3n\pi  \\ x & =-\frac{1}{2}+3n.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the expression giving all the vertical asymptotes is $x=-\frac{1}{2}+3n,$ where $n$ is an integer.

questions.knowledge_point: Finding a General Expression for the Domain of a Transformed Tangent or Cotangent Function
questions.problem: What is the domain of the function  $f(x)=\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{x}{4}-\frac{\pi }{2})?$ Assume that $n$ is an integer.
questions.worked_solution:
The domain of $y=\operatorname{cot}⁡x$ is given by

$$
x\ne n\pi ,
$$

where $n$ is an integer.

To find the domain of $\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{x}{4}-\frac{\pi }{2}),$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $(\frac{x}{4}-\frac{\pi }{2}).$ This gives

$$
\frac{x}{4}-\frac{\pi }{2}\ne n\pi .
$$

Solving for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{4}-\frac{\pi }{2} & \ne n\pi  \\ \frac{x}{4} & \ne \frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi  \\ x & =2\pi +4n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the domain of the function is $x\ne 2\pi +4n\pi ,$ where $n$ is an integer.

questions.problem: What is the domain of the function $f(x)=3\operatorname{tan}⁡(3x+\frac{\pi }{6})+1?$ Assume that $n$ is an integer.
questions.worked_solution:
The domain of $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡x$ is given by

$$
x\ne \frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi ,
$$

where $n$ is an integer.

To find the domain of $3\operatorname{tan}⁡(3x+\frac{\pi }{6})+1,$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $(3x+\frac{\pi }{6}).$ This gives

$$
3x+\frac{\pi }{6}\ne \frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi .
$$

Solving for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3x+\frac{\pi }{6} & \ne \frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi  \\ 3x & \ne \frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi -\frac{\pi }{6} \\ 3x & \ne \frac{\pi }{3}+n\pi  \\ x & \ne \frac{\pi }{3\cdot 3}+\frac{n\pi }{3} \\ x & \ne \frac{\pi }{9}+\frac{n\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the domain of the function is $x\ne \frac{\pi }{9}+\frac{n\pi }{3},$ where $n$ is an integer.

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Finding a General Expression for the Zeros of a Transformed Tangent or Cotangent Function
canonical_examples.problem: Which expression gives all of the zeros of the function $f(x) = \cot \left(2x + \dfrac \pi 6\right)?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The zeros of $y=\cot x$ are given by

$$
x = \dfrac{\pi}{2} + n\pi,
$$

where $n$ is an integer.

To find the zeros of $f(x) = \cot \left(2x + \dfrac \pi 6\right),$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $\left(2x + \dfrac \pi 6\right).$ This gives

$$
2x + \dfrac \pi 6 =  \dfrac{\pi}{2} + n\pi.
$$

Solving for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+\frac{\pi }{6} & =\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi  \\ 2x & =\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi -\frac{\pi }{6} \\ 2x & =\frac{\pi }{3}+n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{\pi }{6}+\frac{n\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the zeros are $x = \dfrac{\pi}{6} + \dfrac{n\pi}{2},$ where $n$ is an integer.

canonical_examples.problem: What is the domain of the function $y=\tan\left(\dfrac x 2\right)?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The domain of $y=\tan x$ is given by the expression

$$
x \neq \dfrac\pi 2 + n\pi ,
$$

where $n$ is an integer.

To find the domain of $\tan\left(\dfrac x 2\right),$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $\left(\dfrac x 2\right).$ This gives

$$

$$

$$

Therefore, the domain of the function is $x \neq \pi + 2n\pi,$ where $n$ is an integer.
